This means the flow processes identified information for at least one and likely multiple individuals.
assumptions: Assumes the invite flow uses direct identifiers such as email address, phone number, or account/account-holder identifiers.

title: Invitation links parent, child, and secondary guardian relationship data
description: The invite operation creates or conveys a relationship between different individuals: the parent initiating the invite, the child whose location will be shared, and the invited secondary guardian. This combination of data links records across individuals and reveals family or caregiving relationships.
assumptions: Assumes the backend can associate the invitation with a specific child account/profile and the invited guardian identity.

title: Backend stores attributable evidence that parent initiated guardian invitation
description: If the backend records the invitation request, it creates data that can later be used to prove that a specific parent invited a specific secondary guardian to access the child's location. This reduces the parent's ability to deny having performed the action.
assumptions: Assumes normal backend logging or persistence of invitation records.

title: Location-sharing access may be disclosed to an additional dynamically chosen party
description: This flow expands access to the child's location data to a newly invited secondary guardian chosen dynamically by the parent. If the system does not strictly constrain what data the invite grants access to, personal data may become accessible to more parties than functionally necessary or intended.
assumptions: Assumes the invitation results in or facilitates access to the child's location data by the invited guardian.

title: Child may be unaware that location access is being extended to a secondary guardian
description: The flow suggests a parent can invite another person to view the child's location. The child, as data subject, may not be aware that their location data will be disclosed to this additional recipient.
assumptions: Assumes the child is the data subject and the system does not provide effective notice to the child about newly added viewers.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state whether the child receives notice, so applicability depends on product design and the child's role in the service.

title: Sharing child's location with invited guardian may rely on invalid or insufficient consent
description: Granting a secondary guardian access to a child's location is sensitive processing involving a child's personal data and an additional recipient. If the backend accepts the parent's invitation without an appropriate lawful basis or valid consent/authorization framework, the processing may be unlawful.
assumptions: Assumes the jurisdiction or policy requires consent/authorization or another clear lawful basis for sharing a child's location with an additional guardian.
uncertainty_note: Legal applicability depends on jurisdiction, roles of the parties, and the service's chosen lawful basis; the flow alone cannot confirm invalid consent.

title: Linking child and guardian identities through shared live-location access
description: Granting a secondary guardian access to a child's live location explicitly creates and communicates a relationship between the child and that guardian. This enables linking data about different individuals (the child and guardian) within the system context.

title: Secondary guardian can identify the child from shared live location and relationship context
description: The live location is shared specifically with a secondary guardian in the context of guardianship. Even if the payload were not fully identified, the relationship context and revealing attributes make the child readily identifiable to the recipient.

title: Backend creates attributable records of location sharing and access grant
description: The backend's grant of access and transmission of live location are likely to create records that can be attributed to the child and involved guardians, reducing deniability about the sharing relationship and the fact that location data was disclosed.
assumptions: Assumes the backend stores or can reconstruct records of access grants and location-sharing events, which is typical but not explicitly stated.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the system logs or persists sharing events; this is inferred from typical backend behavior rather than stated explicitly.

title: Access grant reveals the child's existence and active association to the secondary guardian
description: By granting access and sharing live location with the secondary guardian, the system response itself reveals that a specific child exists in the system and is associated with that guardian, enabling detection of that relationship and potentially the child's current activity or presence.

title: Live location may disclose more precise location data than functionally necessary
description: Sharing a child's live location with a secondary guardian may expose highly fine-grained, continuously updated location data. Depending on the actual need, this can exceed the minimum granularity necessary for guardianship-related functionality.
assumptions: Assumes 'live location' means precise and frequently updated coordinates rather than coarse location or status.
uncertainty_note: The exact granularity of 'live location' is not specified, so the minimization concern is plausible but not certain.

title: Continuous live-location sharing may occur more frequently than necessary
description: Live location implies repeated or continuous disclosure of the child's whereabouts to the secondary guardian. This frequency of processing may exceed what is functionally necessary for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the feature streams or refreshes location continuously or at short intervals.
uncertainty_note: The flow description says 'live location' but does not specify update interval, so excessive-frequency risk is inferred.

title: Child location is propagated to an additional dynamically assigned party
description: The backend shares the child's live location with a secondary guardian, increasing the number of parties who can access sensitive location data. Because guardians can be granted or changed over time, the receiving party set may be dynamic.
uncertainty_note: If the set of secondary guardians is fixed rather than changeable, Dd.4.1.1 could fit better; dynamic assignment is inferred from the access-grant wording.

title: Child may be unaware that live location is being shared with a secondary guardian
description: The flow indicates that the backend grants a secondary guardian access and shares the child's live location. The child, as data subject, may not be aware of this disclosure or its ongoing nature.
uncertainty_note: The description does not state whether the child is notified or informed, so this threat is based on absence of evidence of transparency.

title: Child may lack control over whether and how live location is shared
description: The backend grants access to a secondary guardian, but no mechanism is described for the child to set preferences, consent boundaries, or limits on the scope and duration of location sharing.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the product's governance and age/consent model; no explicit control mechanism is described.

title: Location sharing with a secondary guardian may rely on invalid or insufficient consent
description: Sharing a child's live location with a secondary guardian is sensitive processing. If the grant is made without valid consent or another proper lawful basis, the processing may be unlawful.
uncertainty_note: The lawful basis is not provided. This is a compliance risk contingent on jurisdiction and consent/governance design.

title: Live-location sharing may violate data minimization requirements
description: Providing live location to a secondary guardian may process more precise or more frequent personal data than necessary for the intended purpose, creating a data minimization compliance risk.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether precise live tracking is strictly necessary for the feature's purpose; the description alone does not establish necessity.

title: Aggregated analytics may still enable group profiling by the partner
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics rather than raw user-level records, the receiving advertising/analytics partner may combine repeated aggregates across segments, time windows, or campaigns to profile groups of users and link observations about one cohort to other related cohorts.
assumptions: Assumes the shared analytics include segmented or repeated aggregate reports rather than a single coarse summary.
uncertainty_note: The flow description says 'aggregated' analytics, which reduces direct linkability; this threat depends on the granularity and repeatability of the aggregates.

title: Small or segmented aggregates could make individuals distinguishable
description: If aggregated usage and engagement analytics are broken down by narrow segments, geography, device type, time period, or campaign, some users may become distinguishable within a very small anonymity set, enabling re-identification by the partner when combined with other data.
assumptions: Assumes aggregates may be segmented finely enough that some cells are small.
uncertainty_note: No explicit evidence of small-cell reporting is given; applicability depends on aggregation thresholds and segmentation choices.

title: Analytics sharing can reveal presence or activity patterns of user cohorts
description: Regular transmission of usage and engagement analytics to an external partner can allow that partner to detect when particular user cohorts, regions, or app features are active, trending, or declining, even without direct identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes the partner receives analytics at a cadence that exposes temporal patterns.
uncertainty_note: This is a cohort-level detecting risk rather than clear individual detection, because the described data is aggregated.

title: Propagation of analytics data to an external partner may exceed what is necessary
description: The backend propagates usage and engagement analytics to an external advertising/analytics partner for monetization of the free tier. This creates a data disclosure risk because personal-data-derived analytics are made accessible to another organization beyond the core service boundary.
assumptions: Assumes the aggregates are derived from personal data and are not strictly necessary to deliver the app's primary functionality.
uncertainty_note: The exact necessity depends on the business model, but sharing with an external monetization partner is clearly described.

title: External partner access increases exposure of analytics-derived personal data
description: By receiving the analytics feed, the advertising/analytics partner becomes an additional predetermined party with access to data derived from user behavior. This increases exposure and the chance of secondary use beyond users' expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the partner is a fixed known recipient for this flow.

title: Users may be unaware that their app behavior is shared for advertising/analytics monetization
description: Data subjects may not realize that backend-generated usage and engagement analytics derived from their app activity are disclosed to an external advertising/analytics partner to fund the free tier.
assumptions: Assumes this sharing is not made prominently clear in the user experience at the time of collection or use.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state whether notice is provided, so this is a plausible but not certain threat.

title: Users may lack meaningful control over analytics sharing with the partner
description: If the backend shares analytics with the advertising/analytics partner by default, data subjects may have no effective preference or consent mechanism to opt out of this secondary processing for monetization.
assumptions: Assumes no granular opt-out or consent control exists for this sharing.
uncertainty_note: Control mechanisms are not described, so applicability depends on actual product settings and consent design.

title: Partner analytics sharing may rely on invalid or absent consent
description: Sharing usage and engagement analytics with an advertising/analytics partner for monetization may be unlawful if it depends on consent that is missing, bundled, not freely given, insufficiently specific, or not informed.
assumptions: Assumes consent is the intended lawful basis or is required in the deployment context for this type of partner sharing.
uncertainty_note: The lawful basis is not stated; if another lawful basis is claimed, a different compliance issue may apply instead.

title: Shared analytics may violate data minimization if more detail is disclosed than needed
description: If the backend sends more granular usage and engagement analytics than necessary to support the stated monetization purpose, the flow may violate the data minimization principle.
assumptions: Assumes the shared aggregates could be reduced further in scope, granularity, or frequency while still serving the business purpose.
uncertainty_note: The description does not specify the granularity or frequency of the analytics, so this is contingent on implementation details.

title: Check-in message and precise location can link multiple events to the same child
description: A manual check-in / SOS message carrying the child's current location is likely associated with a persistent account, device, or parent-child relationship. Even if the payload does not explicitly name the child, repeated submissions combined with location and event context can link multiple records to the same child over time.

title: Location and SOS context make the child identifiable
description: The child's current location combined with the SOS/check-in context can act as quasi-identifying information. In many situations, a child's identity can be derived from where they are, when the message was sent, and the known parent-child relationship in the service.

title: SOS/check-in submission can serve as attributable evidence of the child's action
description: The transmitted message constitutes a record that the child initiated a manual check-in or SOS at a particular time and place. This can later be used to attribute the action and make denial difficult.

title: Transmission of SOS/check-in can reveal that the child is active and in a noteworthy situation
description: Observation of this communication can reveal that the child is currently using the service and may be in a situation prompting a manual check-in or SOS. The existence and timing of the message itself can therefore be privacy-sensitive.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether an observer can see the communication metadata or infer the event from traffic patterns; the flow description alone does not specify transport protections.

title: Current location may be disclosed at finer granularity than necessary
description: Sending the child's current location to the backend for a manual check-in / SOS may disclose highly precise location data. Depending on the functional need, exact coordinates may be more fine-grained than necessary to support the parent notification use case.
uncertainty_note: The description says 'current location' but does not specify whether this is exact GPS coordinates or a coarser area, so granularity risk is inferred.

title: Child may be unaware of backend processing and downstream use of SOS/location data
description: Once the child sends the manual check-in / SOS with location, the backend may store, analyze, or forward that data beyond the immediate act of notifying the parent. If these processing steps are not transparent, the child may be unaware of how their sensitive location and emergency-context data are handled.
uncertainty_note: The flow description confirms transmission to the backend but does not explicitly state what subsequent processing occurs.

title: Potential data minimization non-compliance from collecting precise child location in SOS/check-in flow
description: This flow processes sensitive child location data in connection with a manual check-in / SOS. If the backend collects more precise or richer location/context data than strictly necessary for the feature, the processing may violate the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: A compliance issue exists only if the implementation collects more data than necessary; the flow description alone does not confirm the exact scope of collected fields.
